This appeal is filed by the claimants in O.P (Mv) No.914 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accidents
Claims Tribunal, Muvattupuzha, filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, "the Act"), claiming compensation.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimants is that on 19.11.2006, at about 11.30 a.m., while the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KL-17/C 2751 through Muvattupuzha Thodupuzha public road, a car bearing Reg. No. KL6/A 970 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner,
collided with the motorcycle.
As a result of the impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries, and later succumbed to the said injuries.

The claimants approached MACA NO.2248 OF 2013 : 4 :
2025:KER:94713 the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 4,00,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 to 3, were the owner, driver and the insurer of the offending vehicle and respondents 4 and 5 were the owner and the insurer of the motorcycle, respectively.
Before the tribunal, respondents 1, 2 and 4 were set ex parte.
The third respondent, insurer of the car, filed a written statement contending that the policy in favour of the first respondent is only for the period from 18.11.2006 to 17.11.2007.
It is further contending that the accident was not due to the negligent act of the driver of the car.
The fifth respondent insurer of the motorcycle filed a written statement admitting the policy but denying the liability.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A11, B1 and X1 were marked.
The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, dismissed the claim petition filed by the petitioners.
Challenging the dismissal of the claim petition, the claimants have come up in appeal.

A memo dated 13.11.2025 was filed MACA NO.2248 OF 2013 : 5 :
2025:KER:94713 to record the death of the first appellant.
Memo recorded; his legal heirs/appellants 2 and 3 are already in the party array.

4. Heard the learned Counsel for the appellants and the learned Standing Counsel for the third respondent- insurer.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the tribunal dismissed the original petition on the ground that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased/ rider of the motorcycle.
For the purpose of arriving at the said conclusion, the tribunal relied upon the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Sinitha [2011 (4) KLT 821 (SC)].

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Sinitha [2011 (4) KLT 821 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was further submitted that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar and another [2017(4) KLT 1093] held that negligence may not be looked into in a case filed under Section 163A of the Act and argued that the claimants are MACA NO.2248 OF 2013 : 6 :
2025:KER:94713 entitled for compensation.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar and another [2017(4) KLT 1093]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I find force in the said argument.

Since the claim petition is filed under Section 163A of the Act, following the judgment of the Apex Court in Sunil Kumar (supra) and the larger bench decision of this court in Suresh v. Vasantha Shetty [2025 (5) KHC 520], wherein it was held that adjudication under S.163A is required to be made without any requirement of proof of negligence of the driver / owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and therefore negligence Sasi P.T vs C.T.Mathew on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194902618/
3 need not be considered.

In the present case, the deceased, the rider of the motorcycle,
steps into the shoes of the owner and hence, the insurer of the motorcycle cannot be held liable to pay compensation for his death.

Under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the principle of no-fault liability applies; however, as another vehicle-- namely, a car, was involved in the accident, and thus, the insurer of the car becomes liable to pay the compensation.

Therefore, the 3rd respondent/insurer of the car is liable to MACA NO.2248 OF 2013 : 7 :
2025:KER:94713 pay the compensation.
6. The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the monthly income claimed was 3,000/-.
7. As per the Second Schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act, since the income was fixed as 3,000/- and the deceased was aged 23 years, the total compensation payable is 6,48,000/-.
However, 1/3rd of the income has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, as per the Second Schedule.
Accordingly, after deducting 1/3 rd of the income from 6,48,000/-, the appellants will be entitled to get a compensation of 4,32,000/- (6,48,000 x 2/3).
The learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that the tribunal did not award any amount under the heads funeral expenses, loss of estate and medical expenses.

Accordingly, as per the Second Schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act, I find that the claimants are entitled for an amount of 2,000/- towards funeral expenses, 2,500/- MACA NO.2248 OF 2013 : 8 :
2025:KER:94713 towards loss of estate and 15,000/- towards medical expenses,
respectively.

Accordingly, the total compensation payable to the appellants is 4,51,500/- (4,32,000 + 2,000 + 2,500 + 15000).
8.
Since the appeal is of the year 2013, I fix the interest on the enhanced compensation @ 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part.

The appellants 2 and 3 are awarded a total compensation of 4,51,500/- (Rupees Four lakhs fifty one thousand five hundred only) with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.
The 3rd respondent/insurer of the car shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The appellants 2 and 3 shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, AADHAAR Card and bank details before the MACA NO.2248 OF 2013 : 9 :
2025:KER:94713 tribunal within a period of one month so as to enable the third respondent to make the deposit as ordered above.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellants 2 and 3 at the earliest in accordance with law.
